If you like numbers going up, weird builds, and absolutely destroying trees with questionable engineering decisions, this game is dangerously addictive. There’s actually a surprising amount of build variety here. Every run turns into “okay one more try” because you unlock some new f***ing awesome combo and suddenly your screen becomes pure chaos. The progression feels satisfying without becoming a spreadsheet simulator. Also… the price? Honestly feels illegal. I genuinely feel like I robbed the developer. This could easily cost more with the amount of content and replayability packed into it. Came for “hehe chop tree,” stayed because my range build turned into a nuclear logging operation. Highly recommended for roguelike enjoyers and anyone who likes experimenting with broken/fun builds.

I have been waiting for this game and i can say it was worth it

Charming, whimsical, and very fun. A typical run starts a little slow - just your beaver employee of choice and their trusty teeth - but gradually ramps up as you acquire and upgrade your tools. You know: axes, interns, anvils, elephants, giant burrowing worms, golfballs, missiles, tennis machines, penguins... by the latter shifts you'll be tearing through the tree like it's made of paper! If you play your cards right, that is, because there is some strategy to this. Just enough to keep you from drifting off with the wonderful music. Or being eaten by bats, or worse, fired. It's great. Play it when you want to play something simple and fun. Or if you have a debt to a bunch of shady imps that can only be paid off with ten days and nights of chomping timber. Either works!

Timber fever is a great game, I really dig the concept. There's a lot of love behind the game and you can really tell, be it by the frequent updates or frequent references here and there. I would love to see more boss monsters and some voicelines for what I call "Timber Time" (when you get 2x timber), as well as some sound effects for Cherry's dash for example, but overall the game feels complete and really fun to play while queueing for something else. Game runs smooth as butter, and I really appreciate that you can just hold the bite button instead of having to spam it! ALSO INSANELY GOOD VALUE FOR MONEY
Love cutting down trees, now I don't need to find a new tree every time with this infinitely tall tree. Love the peace sign weapon. Fun game.
I like it! I dont know why but these kind of games just tickle my brain in the right places. Number go up, brain go YES MORE!

In my opinion Timber Fever has a lot of excellent qualities: the gameplay is relaxing but still engaging, the progression is rewarding, the learning curve is well-designed, it features a charming art-style and theme, and you can break the game with many different builds which keeps it fresh for quite some time. The only criticism I have is that some weapons are clearly much stronger than others, so you could call that a bit unbalanced, but then again, that is also part of what makes a roguelite fun: some runs you get to take it easy after hitting an extremely broken build, and other runs you have to put in more effort because you didn't get so lucky. So is it even a criticism? I don't know, you decide Overall, I find this game to be great fun, and I'm honestly surprised that it has so few reviews after being out for almost a week (only 19 at the time of writing). For anyone interested in these types of games, I definitely recommend giving it a try.

I was already a big fan of the demo version, and the full game definitely lived up to my expectations. The gameplay is simple but super addictive, with fast-paced action that keeps you hooked for "just one more round". The visuals are charming, the controls feel smooth and it's the kind of game that is easy to pick up but hard to put down. Definitely worth buying!

Idle & Incremental Lovers recommends Timber Fever: [i] Pixel art woodcutting fiesta enjoyable in short sessions due to its repetitive side. Tools (weapons) and upgrades are interesting and choices really matter. Pricy unlocks make it too grindy, though. [/i] + Many baddies on screen :-) + Great rewards "no hit" shifts, so you're incentified to focus on what's happening. + You actually have to use your brainpower when choosing tools (weapons) and perks (what, you're saying I have to use my brain in an incremental game???). +/- Multiple playable beavers, but they don't feel so different from each other. - You only go left and right, plus attack/cut. And a not very impactful special. Even playing only one run par gaming session feels repetitive. - The game overstays its welcome. Unlocking new tools, perks and beaver is too grindy & going through the 5 difficulty levels doesn't bring enough novelty to feel worth playing. - No controller support. It's a matter of personal preference, but I think it would be much more comfortable with it. *The beaver in my local zoo is quite the celebrity. His name is Clint.
